extra.message: Both the `filter` and `query` path parameters from GET /v1/search/:filter/:query are concatenated directly into a SQL string that is passed to db.sequelize.query(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. /v1/search/id/1' OR '1'='1) leading to full SQL injection and database compromise.

The `brand` path parameter is concatenated into a shell command executed with child_process.execSync(). Payloads such as `bud | whoami` or `; cat /etc/passwd` execute arbitrary OS commands on the server (remote code execution).

POST /v1/init passes the attacker-controlled `req.body.object` to node-serialize's unserialize(). node-serialize executes functions marked with the `_$$ND_FUNC$$_` marker, so a crafted body results in remote code execution during deserialization.

The uploaded XML file is parsed with libxmljs using {noent: true}, which resolves external entities. An attacker can define an external entity referencing local files (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) or internal services, resulting in file disclosure / SSRF (XXE).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The `picture` query parameter is used unsanitized to build `../../../uploads/${filename}` and then read with fs.readFile(path.join(__dirname, filePath)). A value such as `../.env` (documented in the JSDoc) escapes the uploads directory and reads arbitrary files from the server.

GET / passes the attacker-controlled `req.query.message` to nunjucks.renderString(), which compiles and evaluates it as a template. Payloads such as {{range.constructor("return global.process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id')")()}} achieve server-side template injection and remote code execution.
GET /register likewise passes the attacker-controlled `req.query.message` to nunjucks.renderString(), allowing server-side template injection and remote code execution.

The message rendered from user-controlled req.query.message on GET / is output with the `| safe` filter, disabling autoescaping. A payload like /?message=<script>alert(0)</script> (shown in the route's JSDoc) is reflected into the HTML and executed in the victim's browser.

The user's `address` field is rendered with the `| safe` filter, disabling autoescaping. Address is attacker-controlled (set via registration or PUT /v1/user/:id), so a stored script payload is persisted and executed whenever the profile is viewed.

GET /v1/test/ takes the `url` query parameter and passes it directly to axios.get(). There is no allowlist or validation, so an attacker can make the server issue requests to internal resources (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) for SSRF.

GET /v1/redirect/ passes the attacker-controlled `url` query parameter directly to res.redirect() with no validation, allowing an open redirect to an arbitrary external site (e.g. /v1/redirect/?url=https://evil.example).

A hardcoded JWT secret fallback ("superSecretPassword") is embedded in source. Additionally, the `|` bitwise operator is used instead of `||`, so the environment variable is ignored and the expression always evaluates to the literal, meaning JWTs are signed with a known constant.
The express-session middleware uses a hardcoded secret ('SuperSecret'), allowing anyone with source access to forge or tamper with signed session cookies.
The JWT signing secret is hardcoded as "SuperSecret" inside the login/token handlers instead of using the configured secret, enabling attackers to forge valid tokens.

The session `genid` returns a deterministic, predictable value (req.session.uid + "_" + 123 / timestamp) rather than a cryptographically random identifier. Session IDs are guessable and not regenerated on login, enabling session fixation and hijacking.
The session cookie is configured with httpOnly: false and secure: false, so it is accessible to JavaScript (enabling theft via XSS) and transmitted over plaintext HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: verifyToken uses jwt.decode() instead of jwt.verify(), so the token signature is never validated. An attacker can supply an arbitrary/forged JWT and have req.userId set to any value, bypassing authentication. (The commented-out jwt.verify call confirms the intended behavior was removed.)

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: GET /v1/user/:id has no authentication or authorization and returns any user's record (including password) by iterating the id, a classic IDOR / broken object level authorization.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DELETE /v1/user/:id performs an unauthenticated user deletion. Any anonymous client can delete arbitrary users by id (broken function level authorization).

PUT /v1/user/:id passes the entire req.body directly into db.user.update(), allowing mass assignment of any column (e.g. role:'admin') for any user id without authentication, resulting in horizontal and vertical privilege escalation.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: PUT /v1/admin/promote/:id sets role='admin' for an arbitrary user with no authentication or admin check, allowing any anonymous attacker to grant themselves admin privileges.
GET /profile trusts the `id` query parameter and renders any user's profile without verifying the requester is authenticated or the owner of that account (IDOR / broken object level authorization).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /v1/admin/new-beer/ is registered with no authentication/authorization middleware despite being an admin-only operation, so any anonymous user can create inventory records.
POST /v1/admin/upload-pic/ accepts file uploads via multer with no authentication and no file type/extension validation, allowing arbitrary files (potentially executable) to be written to ./uploads/.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: POST /v1/admin/new-beer-xml/ is registered with no authentication/authorization middleware, exposing the XXE parser to anonymous attackers.
GET /v1/admin/users/ serializes all user model fields, including the password column, to the API response. Sensitive credential data is exposed to any caller with a token.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: GET /v1/order eagerly includes the `users` association, returning full user objects (including password hashes and PII) for every beer. This is an unauthenticated endpoint, so sensitive user data is over-exposed.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: POST /v1/user/login responds with the entire user record (res.status(200).json(user)), including the password hash, exposing credentials to the client.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Registration stores passwords using MD5 (md5(userPassword)), a fast, collision-prone hash unsuitable for password storage. It is trivially brute-forced/rainbow-tabled.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The email validation regex uses nested quantifiers ((...)+\@((...)+\.)+(...)+) which exhibit catastrophic backtracking. A crafted long input such as aaaaa...@aaaa...{ (documented in the route JSDoc) pins the event loop and causes denial of service.

The OTP check `if(isValid || userToken == req.session.otp)` contains a logic flaw: the generated OTP is stored into the attacker's own session and any matching value passes, and the seed is user-controlled. This allows authentication to be completed without knowing a legitimate OTP (broken 2FA).
POST /v1/user/token returns 404 with 'User was not found' for unknown emails but 401 for wrong passwords, letting an attacker enumerate valid accounts.
checkRolesExisted loops over the attacker-controlled req.body.roles array without a length bound, so a very large array forces excessive CPU work and can degrade/deny service.
